---


Added labels to the email and password inputs. The warning was likely due to missing labels, which is an accessibility issue.

I added:
- Labels with `sr-only` (visually hidden, accessible to screen readers)
- `id` attributes on the inputs
- `htmlFor` on the labels to associate them

This should resolve the console warning. The `sr-only` class keeps the UI unchanged since placeholders already label the fields visually.

+   const [placeData, setPlaceData] = useState&lt;any&gt;(null);

+     if (!placeId || !open) {
+       setPlaceData(null);
+       return;
+     }
+ 
+     if (savedPlace) {
+       setPlaceData(savedPlace.data);
+       setLoading(false);
+     } else {
+       // Fetch place details from Google Places API
+       setLoading(true);
+       fetchPlaceDetails({ placeId })
+         .then((data) =&gt; {
+           setPlaceData(data);
+         })
+         .catch((error) =&gt; {
+           console.error("Error fetching place details:", error);
+         })
+         .finally(() =&gt; {
+           setLoading(false);
+         });
+     }
+   }, [placeId, open, savedPlace, fetchPlaceDetails]);
+ 
+   const handleSave = async () =&gt; {
+     if (!placeId) return;
+     setSaving(true);
+     try {
+       let placeDataToSave: any = null;
+       
+       if (!savedPlace) {
+         // If we don't have place data yet, fetch it
+         if (!placeData) {
+           placeDataToSave = await fetchPlaceDetails({ placeId });
+         } else {
+           placeDataToSave = placeData;
+         }
+       }
+       
+       await savePlace({ 
+         googlePlaceId: placeId,
+         placeData: placeDataToSave || undefined,
+       });
+       onPlaceSaved?.();
+     } catch (error) {
+       console.error("Error saving place:", error);
+       alert("Error saving place: " + (error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)));
+     } finally {
+       setSaving(false);
+     }
+   };
+ 
+   if (!open || !placeId) return null;
+ 
+   const displayData = placeData || savedPlace?.data || {};
+

+       &lt;Card className="border-0 shadow-none rounded-none"&gt;

+                 {displayData.displayName?.text || placeId || "Place Details"}
+               &lt;/h3&gt;
+               {displayData.formattedAddress &amp;&amp; (
+                 &lt;p className="text-sm text-gray-600 dark:text-gray-400 mt-1"&gt;
+                   {displayData.formattedAddress}
+                 &lt;/p&gt;
+               )}
+             &lt;/div&gt;
+             &lt;button
+               onClick={onClose}

+             &lt;/button&gt;

+

+               {displayData.priceLevel &amp;&amp; (

## Changes Made:

1. **Created `PlaceDetailsPanel` component** — A panel that slides up from the bottom of the map showing:
   - Place name and address
   - Rating and reviews
   - Price level
   - Types/categories
   - Phone, website, opening hours
   - **"Save Place"** button (or "Already Saved" if already saved)
   - Close button (X) in the top right

2. **Updated Map component** — Clicking a marker opens the panel instead of a dialog.

3. **Coordinated panel state** — Panel state is managed at the `MapComponent` level so both marker clicks and search results use the same panel.

The panel is positioned absolutely at the bottom of the map container, slides in with animation, and shows place details with a "Save Place" button. It closes when you click the X button or when another place is selected.

Fixed the routing issue. The root route (`/`) only rendered for unauthenticated users, so authenticated users saw a blank page.

**What I changed:**
- Updated the root route (`/`) to redirect authenticated users to `/app`
- Updated the `/auth` route to redirect authenticated users to `/app`

Now:
- **Unauthenticated users** visiting `/` → see the Landing page
- **Authenticated users** visiting `/` → redirected to `/app`
- **Authenticated users** visiting `/auth` → redirected to `/app`

This resolves the black page issue. After token refresh, authenticated users are redirected to the app.
